questions.prompt: Solara Fixtures' primary ledger has been live for two years, and a controller wants to change its functional currency from USD to EUR because the parent company now prefers EUR reporting. What actually happens?
options: The change is not possible — once a ledger is saved, its chart of accounts, calendar, and currency are locked, because changing them would make historical balances incomparable to new ones
Oracle allows the change immediately, since currency is the one ledger component that can always be edited after save
The change is possible, but only after every historical journal is manually re-entered in EUR
The change requires creating a new secondary ledger, which then automatically replaces the primary ledger's currency going forward
questions.explain: Lesson 1 establishes that once a ledger is saved, its chart of accounts, calendar, and currency are locked — only the accounting method can still be changed later. Changing currency after two years of history would make old and new balances incomparable, which is exactly what the lock is designed to prevent.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Oracle Fusion General Ledger summarizes posted journal lines into a pre-aggregated, multidimensional structure called the ________, which is why account inquiries and the trial balance return instantly instead of re-scanning every journal line.
questions.explain: Lesson 2 describes the balances cube as the summarized, multidimensional structure posting updates along every dimension — account, period, currency, balance type — so reports and inquiries read pre-aggregated numbers instead of re-totaling raw journal detail.

questions.prompt: Match each term from Chapter 1 to what it actually is.
right: Controls which ledgers (or ledger sets) a user can access, and optionally which balancing segment values within them
A real registered entity that can sign a contract, sue, or be sued
Holds the actual chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting method
An operational grouping of activity, like sales or purchasing, that reports its accounting results to a specific ledger
questions.explain: A legal entity is the real registered entity that can sign a contract, sue, or be sued. A business unit is an operational grouping of activity reporting to a specific ledger. A ledger holds the actual chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting method. A data access set controls which ledgers and balancing segment values a user can access.

questions.prompt: Put these five period statuses in the order a period normally moves through, from Lesson 4.
items: Never Opened
Future Enterable
Open
Closed
Permanently Closed
questions.explain: A period almost always moves through this sequence in order: Never Opened, then Future Enterable (subledger entry allowed but not GL posting), then Open (full entry and posting), then Closed (no new postings, can be reopened), and finally Permanently Closed (locked for good).

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes what must be true before a manual journal in Oracle Fusion General Ledger is eligible to post?
options: It must have passed validation (balanced, valid accounts, no cross-validation violations), completed any required approval workflow, and have an accounting date in a period with Open status
It only needs to balance — approval and period status don't affect whether a journal can post
It must be posted within the same session it was created in, or it reverts to Incomplete
It must be flagged for AutoPost, since only AutoPost-eligible journals can actually post
It must have a control total entered, since Oracle requires one for every batch before posting
It must be dated in a Future Enterable period, since posting always targets the next period rather than the current one
questions.explain: Lesson 10 lists three conditions together: the journal must pass validation, complete its approval workflow (or need none), and carry an accounting date in a period with Open status. All three have to hold at once — posting eligibility isn't just about the numbers matching.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B keeps the balancing requirement from Lesson 6 right, but drops the other two gates Lesson 10 is specifically built on: a validated, balanced journal still cannot post if it's awaiting approval, and it cannot post if its accounting date falls in a period that isn't Open. Posting eligibility requires all three conditions together, not just the balance check.

questions.prompt: Solara Fixtures has a cross-validation rule blocking Cost Center 500 (EU Sales) from ever combining with Company 01 (US). A preparer enters a journal line using Cost Center 500 and Company 01 — both of which are individually valid, active values. What happens when they try to complete the journal?
options: The journal fails validation with a cross-validation rule violation, even though both segment values are individually valid, because the specific pairing is disallowed
The journal completes normally, since cross-validation rules only apply to disabled account combinations, not valid ones
Oracle silently reassigns the line to Company 02 instead of rejecting it
The journal completes, but the line is automatically routed to a suspense account
questions.explain: Lesson 9 defines a cross-validation rule as blocking a combination of individually-valid segment values that shouldn't be paired together. Both 500 and 01 are real, valid values on their own, but the specific pairing is disallowed, so the journal fails validation over that pairing, not over either value being invalid.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about journal sources and categories, per Lesson 7.
options: Every line in a single journal entry must share the same category
A journal's source identifies where it came from (Manual, Payables, Allocation), while its category identifies its business purpose (Accrual, Adjustment)
Most journals in a mature Oracle Fusion environment are created manually by a person, rather than generated by a subledger or GL process
Approval rules and AutoPost criteria sets are commonly scoped to specific sources and categories rather than applying to "all journals"
A journal can mix an Accrual line with a Reclassification line, as long as both lines balance against each other
questions.explain: Every line in a journal must share one category, and source (where it came from) is distinct from category (why it exists). Approval rules and AutoPost criteria commonly target specific source/category pairs. Most journals in a mature environment are actually system-generated by subledgers or GL processes, not typed by hand, and a journal cannot mix categories across its lines — that requires two separate journals.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a ________ is an optional field on a journal batch where you enter the total amount you expect the batch to contain before finishing data entry, so General Ledger can flag a mismatch — like a transposed digit or a missed line — before you complete the batch.
questions.explain: Lesson 8 describes a control total as a self-check: you enter the expected total in advance, and if what you actually entered doesn't match, General Ledger flags the discrepancy before the batch is complete.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of the auto-reverse accrual pattern, from Lesson 11, in the correct order.
items: An accrual journal is created and flagged to reverse automatically in the next period
The accrual journal posts, recording the estimated expense in the current period
The next period opens, and Oracle generates and posts the reversal automatically
The real invoice posts normally through the subledger, with no double counting
questions.explain: Lesson 11's March/April example walks this exact sequence: flag the accrual to auto-reverse, post it in March, let the reversal post automatically when April opens, and then let the real Payables invoice post in April with the accrual's effect already cleanly backed out.

questions.prompt: A journal batch spans three different lines of business, and the company wants every one of those three controllers to sign off before the batch can post — no single controller's approval should be enough on its own. Which assignee type does this?
options: Parallel — every person in the set must approve before the journal can move on
Single — any one person in the group or role can approve
Serial — approvers act one after another in a fixed sequence
AutoPost — the batch posts automatically once validation passes, with no approval at all
questions.explain: Lesson 12 defines Parallel routing as sending a journal to several people at once, where everyone's approval is required — exactly the fit for a batch spanning multiple lines of business that each need their own controller's sign-off, unlike Single (any one approver) or Serial (a fixed sequence).

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about importing journals with FBDI, per Lesson 13.
options: The populated template's rows are first converted to a CSV/zip, then uploaded to WebCenter Content (UCM), before the Import Journals process runs
Journals created through FBDI skip validation, since they were already checked when the file was uploaded
Each row in the GL_INTERFACE template corresponds to one journal line, carrying ledger, accounting date, currency, each chart-of-accounts segment, and a debit or credit amount
Journals imported this way typically carry the source "Spreadsheet," distinguishing them from hand-typed Manual entries
FBDI is specific to General Ledger and isn't used by any other Oracle Fusion Applications module
questions.explain: Lesson 13's five-step flow is template, populate, generate CSV/zip, upload to UCM, then run Import Journals — and each row carries ledger, date, currency, segments, and an amount. Journals created this way carry source "Spreadsheet." FBDI journals still go through the same validation as any other journal before they can post, and FBDI is Oracle's standard bulk-load mechanism used across Fusion Applications generally, not something unique to General Ledger.

questions.prompt: Match each term from journal approvals and AutoPost to what it actually controls.
right: Determines which AutoPost criteria set is evaluated first when more than one could match a batch
Routes to one user, group, or role — any one person in it can approve
Routes to a sequence of approvers one after another, commonly a supervisory chain
Routes to several people at once, and every one of them must approve
questions.explain: Single assignee routes to one approver, or any one person in a group or role. Parallel assignee requires everyone in the set to approve. Serial assignee routes through a sequence, commonly a supervisory chain. AutoPost priority determines which criteria set is evaluated first when more than one could apply.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a row rejected during journal import stays in the ________ table, untouched, with its specific rejection reason attached, until it's corrected and resubmitted.
questions.explain: Lesson 14 explains that rows which fail import-level checks stay in the interface table with their rejection reason attached, while rows that passed become real journal lines — only the rejected rows need correcting and resubmitting, not the whole file.

questions.prompt: Solara Fixtures allocates IT department cost to Sales based on each department's share of total company headcount — a statistic that's already tracked in the ledger. Which recurring journal type fits this, and why?
options: Formula — the amount is calculated from a statistic and an actual balance already in the ledger, so no one needs to type or recalculate anything each period
Standard — the accounts and amount are identical every period, so nothing needs to be calculated
Skeleton — the accounts are fixed, but someone still has to type in this period's amount by hand
Copy Journal — the prior period's journal is duplicated and then manually adjusted
questions.explain: Lesson 17's IT allocation example is exactly a Formula recurring journal: the amount is calculated from a headcount statistic and an actual expense balance already in the ledger, so the number can change period to period without anyone typing or recalculating it.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about allocations and mass allocations, per Lessons 19–20.
options: The allocation formula is: Allocation amount (per target) = Cost Pool × (Target's Usage Factor ÷ Total Usage)
"Mass allocation" means a single rule definition can spread a pool across a whole range of targets, not just a fixed handful
The "basis" in Allocation Manager is the account that relieves the source pool, usually the credit side
A generated allocation journal still has to pass validation and posting like any other journal, with source "Allocation" and category "Allocation"
Adding a new cost center to the business requires rewriting the allocation rule from scratch
questions.explain: The allocation formula and the "mass" range-based targeting are both correct, as is the fact that a generated allocation journal still validates and posts like anything else. The "basis" is the usage driver (like headcount), not the account that relieves the source — that's the "offset." And a mass allocation's range-based targeting means a new cost center can simply be added to the range the rule already sweeps, not a rewrite.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: when you copy a journal with Copy Journal, its status resets to ________, regardless of whether the original journal was posted.
questions.explain: Lesson 21 states that a copied journal's status resets to Incomplete no matter what the original's status was — the copy is a brand-new draft that still has to pass validation and approval before it can post.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of building and running an allocation rule, from Lessons 19–20, in the correct order.
items: Define the allocation rule in Allocation Manager: point of view, source, basis, target, and offset
Run the rule for a specific period, which calculates each target's proportional share of the pool
A journal batch is generated, with source Allocation and category Allocation
The batch goes through the same validation, approval, and posting steps as any other journal
questions.explain: The rule is built once as reusable infrastructure, but running it for a given period is a deliberate action that produces a real journal batch — one that still has to validate, route for approval if applicable, and post, exactly like any other journal.

questions.prompt: At LTV Manufacturing Corporation, a reviewer checks the Utilities Expense balance for March using Inquire on Detail Balances, but accidentally reads the year-to-date figure instead of period-to-date, and concludes the account is overspent for March. What's actually wrong with that conclusion?
options: YTD accumulates every period's activity since the fiscal year began, so it's naturally larger than any single period's figure — the reviewer needs the PTD figure to answer "what did March cost"
YTD and PTD are always identical for expense accounts, so the conclusion is correct regardless of which figure was read
Utilities Expense should never be read as YTD at all, since it isn't a real account
The reviewer should have used Account Monitor instead, since Inquire on Detail Balances can't show YTD figures
questions.explain: Lesson 22 warns that confusing PTD with YTD is one of the most common new-user mistakes. An income statement account like Utilities Expense is normally read PTD to answer "what did this period cost," while YTD answers a different question — how much it has cost so far this fiscal year, which accumulates and will naturally look larger.

questions.prompt: Match each General Ledger tool to the situation it's actually built for, per Lessons 22–25.
right: A formal, point-in-time report confirming debits equal credits, retained as part of the close process
A continuously updated watchlist that flags an account on its own once a defined tolerance is crossed
A deliberate, one-time lookup when you already know exactly which account and period you want
An online, multidimensional pivot tool for slicing a flagged or suspicious balance to find what's really driving it
questions.explain: Inquire on Detail Balances is for a deliberate, one-time lookup. Account Monitor is a self-updating watchlist with tolerances. Account Inspector pivots a flagged or suspicious balance across chart of accounts segments. The Trial Balance Report is the formal, retained report confirming debits equal credits.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the General Ledger Trial Balance Report, per Lesson 25.
options: A trial balance "balancing" proves total debits equal total credits — it does not prove every account was coded or valued correctly
The Begin Year trial balance type is useful for confirming opening balances carried forward correctly
Because Oracle Fusion already enforces balanced journals at entry, a trial balance review itself has nothing left to catch
The income statement and balance sheet are, structurally, the trial balance's accounts regrouped into a different presentation
The Results trial balance type shows balances as of the start of the fiscal year
questions.explain: Balancing only confirms mechanical correctness, not that figures are right — catching things that are "wrong but balanced" is most of what trial balance review actually does, so it has plenty left to catch. Begin Year confirms opening balances. The income statement and balance sheet are the same trial balance data, regrouped. The Results type shows net results for the period, not beginning-of-year balances — that's Begin Year.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a journal report shows what posted; an ________ shows who created, edited, approved, and posted a journal, and when.
questions.explain: Lesson 26 distinguishes journal reports, which show what posted, from the audit trail, which proves who was responsible for each step — creating, editing, approving, posting — and when.

questions.prompt: Put these stops of the drill path from a GL balance to its origin, per Lesson 27, in the correct order.
items: Account balance — a PTD or YTD total for an account combination
Journal lines — the individual lines that sum to that balance
Journal entry or subledger journal entry — the full entry, or the accounting rules that produced it
Subledger transaction — the original business document, like a supplier invoice
questions.explain: Lesson 27 walks this exact path: starting from a summarized balance, drilling into the journal lines behind it, then into the full journal entry (or the subledger journal entry if it came from a subledger), and finally landing on the original business document that started the chain.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes what Period-End Revaluation does, as distinct from Translation?
options: Revaluation restates foreign-currency-denominated balance sheet balances within a single ledger to current period-end rates; Translation restates an entire ledger's balances into a different reporting currency for consolidation
Revaluation restates an entire ledger into a different reporting currency; Translation restates only foreign-currency-denominated balance sheet balances within a single ledger
Revaluation and Translation are two names for exactly the same process, applied at different points in the close
Revaluation only applies to income statement accounts, while Translation only applies to balance sheet accounts
Revaluation permanently changes the original ledger's books, while Translation produces only a temporary, non-posting view
Revaluation runs after Translation each period, since a ledger must already be in the reporting currency before its exposed balances can be restated
questions.explain: Lesson 29 defines revaluation as restating foreign-currency-denominated balance sheet balances within one ledger to current rates, generating a reversing unrealized gain or loss. Lesson 30 defines translation as restating an entire ledger's balances — every account — into a different reporting currency for consolidation. Revaluation runs before translation, not after.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes the two processes with their roles exactly reversed — it's Translation that restates an entire ledger into another reporting currency, and Revaluation that targets only the foreign-currency-denominated balance sheet balances still exposed to rate movement within one ledger. Swapping which process does which job is exactly the mistake the two lessons' careful ordering (revaluation first, then translation) is meant to prevent.

questions.prompt: LTV Manufacturing Corporation books a £8,500 GBP services invoice using the Corporate rate type at 1.27 USD/GBP. What actually updates the USD ledger's functional-currency balance, and what number is it?
options: The accounted amount, $10,795 — the entered £8,500 converted to USD at the Corporate rate
The entered amount, £8,500, converted on the fly every time a report is run
$8,500 — Oracle simply treats the entered number as if it were already in USD
Nothing updates until the invoice is actually paid
questions.explain: Lesson 28's worked example shows exactly this: £8,500 at a Corporate rate of 1.27 USD/GBP produces an accounted amount of $10,795, and it's that accounted amount — not the entered GBP figure — that updates the ledger's functional-currency balance and feeds every report.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about intercompany transactions and consolidation, per Lessons 31–32.
options: Oracle Fusion's intercompany balancing rules automatically generate offsetting receivable/payable lines so each legal entity's own books stay in balance independently
Timing differences and FX rate differences can leave the two sides of an intercompany balance out of sync, which is why an Intercompany Reconciliation Report is run before close
Elimination entries remove intercompany stock ownership, intercompany debt, and intercompany revenue/expense from consolidated results
Reporting-only consolidation is used specifically when entities have different charts of accounts and calendars
An intercompany journal always has every line sharing the same balancing segment value, the same as an ordinary intracompany journal
questions.explain: Intercompany balancing rules auto-generate offsetting lines, reconciliation catches timing/FX mismatches before close, and the three elimination types (stock, debt, revenue/expense) are exactly as described. Reporting-only consolidation is actually used when structures already match — it's balance transfer consolidation that handles different charts of accounts and calendars. And an intercompany journal is defined by crossing different balancing segment values, not sharing one.

questions.prompt: Match each consolidation-related term to what it actually is, per Lessons 30 and 32.
right: Maps and transfers balances when entities have different charts of accounts or calendars
Combines balances directly when structures already match, with far less mapping work
A journal removing the effect of an intra-group transaction from consolidated results
The equity account absorbing the imbalance created by translating balance sheet and income statement lines at two different rates
questions.explain: The CTA is the equity account absorbing the imbalance from using two different translation rates. Reporting-only consolidation combines balances directly when structures already match. Balance transfer consolidation maps and transfers balances when structures differ. An elimination entry removes the effect of an intra-group transaction.

questions.prompt: At LTV Manufacturing Corporation, Payables, Receivables, and Fixed Assets have all completed their own close steps for March, but General Ledger has not yet closed. Why does GL close last in the sequence, rather than first or in parallel?
options: Because GL is where every subledger's activity ultimately lands, so it can't be considered final until everything feeding it is final too
Because GL's close process takes less time than the subledgers', so it's scheduled last purely for convenience
Because Oracle requires GL to close before any subledger, making this scenario already an error
Because GL doesn't actually have a period status of its own — it inherits whichever subledger closes last
questions.explain: Lesson 33 explains the standard closing sequence closes subledgers first and General Ledger last, specifically because GL is where every subledger's activity ultimately lands — it can't be considered final until everything feeding it is final too, and GL remains the one period a controller can still reopen if something is discovered.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: at year-end close, every income statement account's balance for the year is automatically swept into a single balance sheet equity account called ________, triggered by opening the new fiscal year's first period.
questions.explain: Lesson 36 explains that opening the first period of the new fiscal year automatically triggers the sweep of the prior year's net income statement result into Retained Earnings, and resets every income statement account to zero — nobody keys this in manually.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about unposted journals and period status at close, per Lessons 34–35.
options: Oracle Fusion can let a period be closed with unposted journals still sitting in it, but that journal's activity simply isn't in the period's final numbers
A journal stuck awaiting approval, a journal with a failed validation, and a journal that was simply never submitted are all distinct reasons a journal can still be unposted at close time
Generating a recurring journal automatically posts it, so a generated recurring batch is never found sitting unposted at close
A Closed period can still be reopened if something is discovered, but a Permanently Closed period cannot be reopened under any circumstances
Reopening a closed period has no downstream effect on anything that already ran off that period's numbers
questions.explain: A period can close with unposted journals left behind, invisible to the final numbers, for any of several distinct reasons — awaiting approval, failed validation, or never submitted. Closed periods can be reopened; Permanently Closed ones cannot. Generating a recurring journal does not post it automatically, which is exactly why Lesson 34's worked example shows one sitting unposted after generation. Reopening a period is disruptive precisely because reports, reconciliations, and consolidations that already ran off its numbers become stale.

questions.prompt: A Sales division controller at LTV Manufacturing Corporation says March's Travel & Entertainment expense "looks way too high." Put the triage steps from Lesson 37's Scenario 1 in the correct order.
items: Use Inquire on Detail Balances to confirm the actual PTD figure and rule out a PTD/YTD misread
Open Account Inspector and pivot the balance by cost center to see which department is actually driving it
Pull the Account Analysis Report for that cost center to review every journal line posted to it
Drill to subledger detail to see the originating transaction behind any line sourced from a subledger
questions.explain: Lesson 37's Scenario 1 triages from the least invasive tool to the most: confirm the figure with a plain inquiry, pivot with Account Inspector to isolate which cost center is driving it, pull the Account Analysis Report to review the actual journal lines, and only then drill to subledger detail for any line that originated outside GL.
